title: British Indian Army
definition: The British Indian Army was the principal military force of the British Raj, serving as an instrument of colonial expansion, internal security, and imperial defense, characterized by a unique blend of European officer leadership and indigenous rank-and-file soldiers (Sepoys).
importanceInUpsc: Essential for understanding the 'Military-Fiscal State' model, the socio-economic impact of colonial rule, and the structural causes of the 1857 Revolt.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of British Indian Army.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
